a2-past-raah.title: Past Tense: I Went, You Went...
a2-past-raah.pattern: رحت / رحت / رحتي / راح / راحت / رحنا / رحتو / راحو
a2-past-raah.explanation: The past tense of راح (raah, "to go") is formed with suffixes attached to the root ر-و-ح: رحت (riHt, "I went"), رحت (riHt, "you-m went"), رحتي (riHti, "you-f went"), راح (raah, "he went"), راحت (raaHat, "she went"), رحنا (riHna, "we went"), رحتو (riHtaw, "you-all went"), راحو (raaHaw, "they went").
a2-past-raah.fact: Notice the vowel shift: the medial "aa" of راح shortens to a plain "i" in every person except he/she/they (راح/راحت/راحو keep the long "aa"). This a→i shift in all-but-third-person is a very common pattern across Gulf Arabic past-tense verbs, not unique to راح.

dialogue.en: I went home, and I saw the family, good

a2-past-shaaf.title: Past Tense: I Saw, You Saw...
a2-past-shaaf.pattern: شفت / شفت / شفتي / شاف / شافت / شفنا / شفتو / شافو
a2-past-shaaf.explanation: The past tense of شاف (shaaf, "to see") follows the same pattern as راح: شفت (shift, "I saw"), شفت (shift, "you-m saw"), شفتي (shifti, "you-f saw"), شاف (shaaf, "he saw"), شافت (shaafat, "she saw"), شفنا (shifna, "we saw"), شفتو (shiftaw, "you-all saw"), شافو (shaafaw, "they saw").
a2-past-shaaf.fact: Many Emirati speakers pronounce this verb with چ instead of ش (چاف/چفت, chaaf/chift) — a well-known regional sound shift found in parts of the UAE and wider Gulf, and both pronunciations are considered correct.

dialogue.en: Did you (f) see the family yesterday?

dialogue.native: نعم، شفت الأهل، وشفت صديق زين
dialogue.en: Yes, I saw the family, and I saw a good friend

a2-past-negation.title: Negating the Past: Ma + Past Verb
a2-past-negation.explanation: To negate a past-tense verb, put ما (ma) right before it, exactly like with the present tense: ما رحت (ma riHt, "I didn't go"), ما شفت (ma shift, "I didn't see").
a2-past-negation.fact: Unlike the present tense (which splits between ما for verbs and مب for nominal sentences), the past tense always uses ما — there's no مب-equivalent for past-tense negation, which simplifies this pattern compared to the present.

dialogue.en: Did you see the family yesterday?

dialogue.native: لا، ما شفت الأهل، رحت الحين بس
dialogue.en: No, I didn't see the family, I only went now

a2-days-past.title: Days of the Week with Past Tense
a2-days-past.explanation: Combining a day name with a past-tense verb is a natural way to build a simple narrative: يوم الجمعة رحت البيت (yoom el-jum3a riHt el-bayt, "On Friday I went home"). The day name simply comes first, exactly like a time adverb.
a2-days-past.fact: Notice there's no extra preposition needed before the day name ("on Friday") — Emirati, like most Gulf dialects, places time expressions directly at the start of the sentence without a linking word.

items.ar: شفنا هذا أمس، وشفنا كم هذا زين اليوم
items.en: We saw this yesterday, and we saw how much this is, good, today
items.translit: shifna hatha ams, wa shifna kam hatha zayn el-yoom

lessons.title: Big and Small in the Past

items.ar: شفت بيت كبير أمس، وشفت بيت صغير اليوم
items.en: I saw a big house yesterday, and I saw a small house today
items.translit: shift bayt kabeer ams, wa shift bayt sagheer el-yoom

items.ar: شاف بيت جديد أمس، وشاف بيت قديم اليوم
items.en: He saw a new house yesterday, and he saw an old house today
items.translit: shaaf bayt jideed ams, wa shaaf bayt gadeem el-yoom

items.ar: شافت بيت كبير وجديد أمس، زين والحمد لله
items.en: She saw a big, new house yesterday, good, thank God
items.translit: shaafat bayt kabeer wa jideed ams, zayn wal-hamdulillah

items.ar: شفنا بيت صغير وقديم أمس، بس زين اليوم
items.en: We saw a small, old house yesterday, but it's good today
items.translit: shifna bayt sagheer wa gadeem ams, bas zayn el-yoom

items.ar: يوم الأحد رحت البيت، والبيت قريب وكبير زين

items.translit: yoom el-a7ad riHt el-bayt, wal-bayt gareeb wa kabeer zayn

items.ar: راح البيت أمس، وشفت هذا اليوم، غالي كثير

items.translit: raaH el-bayt ams, wa shift hatha el-yoom, ghaali katheer

items.ar: شفنا بيت جديد أمس، وشفنا الفلوس اليوم زين
items.en: We saw a new house yesterday, and we saw the money today, good
items.translit: shifna bayt jideed ams, wa shifna el-fluus el-yoom zayn

items.ar: شافو بيت صغير أمس، وشافو صديق زين اليوم
items.en: They saw a small house yesterday, and they saw a good friend today
items.translit: shaafo bayt sagheer ams, wa shaafo sadeeq zayn el-yoom

items.ar: أشرب قهوة اليوم، وأمس شفت الأهل زين
items.en: I drink coffee today, and yesterday I saw the family, good
items.translit: ashrab gahwa el-yoom, wa ams shift el-ahl zayn

items.ar: يشرب شاي اليوم، وأمس راح البيت زين
items.en: He drinks tea today, and yesterday he went home, good
items.translit: yishrab shaay el-yoom, wa ams raaH el-bayt zayn

items.ar: تشرب مويه اليوم، وأمس شافت صديق زين
items.en: She drinks water today, and yesterday she saw a good friend
items.translit: tishrab moya el-yoom, wa ams shaafat sadeeq zayn

items.ar: نشرب قهوة اليوم، وأمس رحنا البيت زين
items.en: We drink coffee today, and yesterday we went home, good

items.ar: أنا تعبان اليوم، بس أمس شفت الأهل زين

items.ar: هو مبسوط اليوم، وأمس راح البيت والحمد لله
items.en: He's happy today, and yesterday he went home, thank God
items.translit: huwa mabsoot el-yoom, wa ams raaH el-bayt wal-hamdulillah

items.ar: هي جوعان اليوم، بس أمس شافت صديق زين

items.ar: احنا عطشان اليوم، بس أمس رحنا البيت زين

items.ar: شفت أبويه أمس، ويشرب قهوة زين اليوم

items.ar: شفت يمة أمس، وتشرب شاي زين اليوم

items.ar: الأهل زين اليوم، وشفت الأهل أمس والحمد لله

items.translit: el-ahl zayn el-yoom, wa shift el-ahl ams wal-hamdulillah

items.ar: شنو شفت أمس؟ شفت بيت كبير وجديد

items.translit: shinu shift ams? shift bayt kabeer wa jideed

items.ar: وين رحت أمس؟ رحت البيت زين والحمد لله

items.translit: wein riHt ams? riHt el-bayt zayn wal-hamdulillah

items.ar: ليش راح أمس؟ ما أدري، بس راح زين

items.ar: رحت البيت أمس، وشفت الأهل، والحمد لله زين
